maria ramos: Quick FYI I opened a docs PR to clarify streaming + Optimize Toolkit interactions and to replace several outdated SDK snippets and broken internal links. The old Python example didn't show the streaming handler with batching semantics and we have no guidance on which quant profiles are safe for streaming. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/910

linh tran: Nice — thanks for taking this on. Can you summarize the main user-facing changes in the PR?

maria ramos: Sure. High level: 1) add a Python streaming example that uses ContinuousBatcher + a streaming callback so readers can see how to interleave token streaming with background KV prefetching; 2) add a short note about quant profile compatibility with streaming (recommend "shortseq" or the new "stream-friendly" profile where available); 3) replace external gist links with internal example paths so docs extraction works; 4) small perf mini-table (illustrative) and a runnable microbench command.

tomas k.: For the quant profile note, can we be explicit about regressions? e.g., some heavy-quantized 4-bit profiles can drop token emission behavior (stuttering) in streaming — should call that out.

maria ramos: Good point. I'll add a caution: "Aggressive quantization (eg 4-bit schemes) can increase token latency jitter in streaming; prefer stream-friendly or shortseq profiles for real-time streaming apps."

devex-ana: UX suggestion: show a tiny before/after table and a minimal `curl`/`python` command so readers can reproduce quickly. Keep it short, 2 rows only.

maria ramos: Will add. Proposed runnable microbench: `python -m examples.optimize.stream_bench --profile=stream-friendly --batch=continuous`

maria ramos: Draft Python streaming snippet (short):
```python
from redwood import Client
from redwood.optimize import ContinuousBatcher, WithKVPrefetch, WithQuantProfile

client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
cb = ContinuousBatcher(client, prefetch=WithKVPrefetch())

# streaming handler
async def on_token(tok):
    print(tok, end="", flush=True)

# start generation (streaming)
await cb.generate_stream("Summarize: ...", on_token=on_token, quant_profile=WithQuantProfile("stream-friendly"))
```

linh tran: nice and clear. Please add a one-line fallback explanation: if KV prefetch misses we still serve via the single-request path but streaming p95 can increase ~1.6-2x.

maria ramos: added fallback note. Also replaced all external links with `/examples/optimize/streaming/*` internal paths and fixed a broken crosslink to `/optimize/quant-profiles` that used an old slug.

tomas k.: CI note: the docs snip extractor expects language fences to match the internal path tag. Make sure the code fence has "```python" and the snippet extraction comments are present. I left a small PR comment about that.
